audience: DCCE (กรม สส.) executives and policy owners reading the Executive Summary Report
decision_use: Understand why A-BTR is the department's core mandate and strategic goal, and how the A-BTR-specific knowledge/data gap threatens it and what closing it requires
section_job: Explain A-BTR's importance as the department's core mission and strategic goal -- developing a service that supports A-BTR compilation simultaneously upgrades the data platform and website content -- explain the A-BTR-specific knowledge/data gap and its impact. Stays scoped to A-BTR itself: does NOT carry the general whole-website content-gap statistic (that is 4.1's figure) and does NOT conclude with the four institutional roles (that conclusion belongs to 4.4, the plan's dedicated governance/Product-Owner section) -- Boss corrected both scope errors directly on the plan-slice, 2026-08-30
target_altitude: Executive narrative grounded in A-BTR-specific figures where available (e.g. the A-BTR-linked subset of content/data gaps), no per-field metadata
report_specific_rules: Full Thai+English agency name at first mention ("กรมการเปลี่ยนแปลงสภาพภูมิอากาศและสิ่งแวดล้อม"), then only "กรม สส." thereafter -- never bare "สส." without "กรม" leading it
Never bare English "NCAIF" -- give the full Thai name at first mention, then use "โครงสร้างข้อมูลด้านการปรับตัวฯ" or "โครงสร้างข้อมูล NCAIF"
No internal jargon abbreviations (TOR70, CRDB) without spelling out at first use

No internal document locators (slide numbers, page numbers, superseded internal section references) in narrative prose -- cite by document name, E-xxx evidence code, or named standard; locators live in evidence-traceability only

Use "คณะที่ปรึกษา" as the active subject for study/survey/interview/workshop/analysis/synthesis/design-decision sentences; avoid passive voice or "โครงการ" as actor except for contractual objective/scope statements
Countable parallel items formatted as numbered/bulleted lists with substantive descriptions, not run-on prose
Executive-summary substance retention: cut operational/technical detail but never reduce a point to one floating sentence; each subsection needs Why/What/So-What in 1-2 paragraphs
Formal official vocabulary ("ข้อมูลอภิพันธ์"/"ข้อมูลกำกับ", "สถาปัตยกรรมสารสนเทศ", "ธรรมาภิบาลข้อมูล"); avoid colloquial phrasing

No contrastive/justify-by-flaw scaffolding -- never justify a point by first negating a bad alternative ("แทนที่จะ...", "เพื่อป้องกัน...", "เพื่อลดความเสี่ยง...", "หลีกเลี่ยง..."); state the A-BTR argument as a direct causal chain (obligation, gap, consequence, role), never as "instead of X, do Y". This is the section where the prior draft's violations of this rule concentrated -- treat it as the primary risk to guard against during verbalization.
inclusions: A-BTR importance as core mission and strategic goal, and how a supporting service upgrades both data platform and website content together

the A-BTR-specific knowledge/data gap Thailand's own BTR2 second interim report admits (Section C, theme data_and_knowledge_gaps, BTR2 SS1.3.2): localized risk/vulnerability data limitations, no standardized Loss and Damage assessment system, absence of outcome indicators, fragmented/non-integrated databases, weak translation of science into practical local tools

the A-BTR reporting-pipeline gap from WP7 Service 9 (CRDB's own independent diagnostic, converging with the BTR2 self-report from the compilation-process angle): hand-compiled figures across agencies with no shared term definitions and poor traceability; 122 report items checked against the catalog, roughly half unmatched; four structural conditions (data/definition gaps, cross-agency coordination, resourcing, monitoring); Gap 10 -- the missing calculation methodology that turns raw data into a reportable figure, not raw data itself
how platform development narrows these A-BTR-specific gaps
exclusions: full enumerated table of the 260 datasets
the whole-website 75-topic content-gap statistic and its 79%/16-26-33 breakdown (belongs to section 4.1)
the four institutional roles / governance-role conclusion (belongs to section 4.4)

the unverified '47 of 75 topics are A-BTR-linked' figure from the prior (archived) run -- checked directly against WP4 Content-Source Gap Analysis v2 and it tags only 5 rows as A-BTR-related; do not reuse this number

WP7's own three institutional roles (standard setter, data authenticator, science-to-decision facilitator) from its Section 7 -- distinct from the plan's four-role Product Owner structure that belongs to section 4.4; do not import either role set into this section
evidence_policy: Evidence base rebuilt from scratch and verified directly against source files, 2026-08-30 (all prior sourcing for this section dropped). Three sources: (1) Section A -- Institutional Baseline, a requirement extraction taken directly from the UNFCCC BTR2 second interim report itself, grounding DCCE's institutional obligation (A-REQ-011, A-REQ-013, A-REQ-018, A-REQ-021); (2) Section C -- Priorities, Barriers and Strategy (requirement items C-020 through C-031, theme data_and_knowledge_gaps, BTR2 SS1.3.2), also extracted directly from the BTR2 report, grounding the A-BTR-specific knowledge/data gap the report itself admits; (3) WP7 Gap Analysis Report Section 5 'Service 9 -- International climate reporting pipeline', CRDB's own independent diagnostic of the same underlying problem from the compilation-process angle. Do not cite WP4 Content-Source Gap Analysis v2 for an A-BTR-linked subset of the 75-topic split -- that figure does not exist in the source. Do not cite the 2026-07-06 BTR M&E use-case draft as independent evidence -- it is an earlier conceptual draft superseded by WP7 Section 5. Keep internal locators and per-source detail in the evidence-traceability sidecar
required_concepts: A-BTR as DCCE's documented institutional obligation (UNFCCC BTR2 second interim report, Section A requirements: lead institutional framework, national focal point/coordination function, DCCE's monitoring/evaluation/reporting coordination role), not external demand

the A-BTR-specific knowledge/data gap the BTR2 report itself admits (Section C, theme data_and_knowledge_gaps): localized risk/vulnerability data limitations, no standardized Loss and Damage assessment system, absence of outcome indicators, fragmented databases, weak science-to-practice translation

WP7 Service 9's reporting-pipeline gap: hand-compilation, missing shared definitions, poor traceability, and Gap 10 (missing calculation methodology) -- CRDB's own independent finding, converging with Section C's self-reported gaps

why A-BTR is strategically complex: compilation spans all four adaptation-cycle stages (climate science, impact/vulnerability/risk assessment, planning and implementation, monitoring/evaluation/learning per NCAIF Sitemap v9 section 3), so every domain's pipeline and data quality must hold -- this is why a data platform (not a single dataset or content page) is the necessary infrastructure, with the website as the layer that then disseminates this content publicly (Boss's own framing, added 2026-08-30)
